title: BA1/2008/2021 of PREETAM SINGH SANDHU Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
 BA1 No.2008 of 2021
Hon'ble R.C. Khulbe, J.
 Mr. Arvind Vashisth, learned senior counsel
for the applicant.
 Mr. Siddhartha Bisht, learned B.H. for the
State.
 Mr. S.K. Mandal, learned counsel for the
informant.
 Applicant-Preetam Singh Sandhu has sought
his release on bail in connection with Case
Crime/FIR No.90/2019, under Sections
306/420/468/471/417/193/201 IPC, registered at
P.S. Nanakmatta, District U.S. Nagar.
 Brief facts of the case are that an FIR was
lodged as per the information of Rishpal Singh that
he along with his brother Jagroop Singh and mother,
since last 18 years, was residing in the Gurudwara
Nanakmatta; he was working as a Sewadar and his
brother Jagroop Singh was also working as a
Sewadar from last 8 years; since the Committee was
formed, his brother Jagroop Singh was harassed by
the applicant Preetam Singh and Kehar Singh by
threatening to remove him as a Sewadar; three
months before the incident, his brother was
removed from the job and he was asked to vacate
the house which was allotted in the precincts of
Gurudwara; due to this pressure, on 14.06.2019, he

committed suicide in the room.
 It is argued that the accused has been falsely
implicated; he is languishing in jail since
02.08.2021; co-accused Kehar Singh has been
enlarged on bail vide order dated 8.3.2021; he is
ready to furnish the sureties and may be granted bail
on parity basis.
Per contra, learned counsel for the State as
also the informant's counsel opposed for bail but
fairly submitted that initially an FIR was lodged u/s
306 IPC; after lodging the FIR, a suicidal note was
recovered from the room of deceased which was
sent for FSL testing; since there was no clear report
about the handwriting of deceased, again the same
was sent to the Central Forensic Science Laboratory
(CFSL), Chandigarh for the verification of
handwriting; all the concerned parties were asked to
send the documents available with them, signed by
the deceased, to verify the handwriting on the
suicidal note; it is alleged that after receipt of
information, the accused prepared a forged
document and sent the same to Chandigarh to
procure the benefit; accordingly, the accused is not
entitled for bail.
On a perusal of the papers available on
record, it appears that after lodging the FIR, a
document was recovered from the room of the
deceased; presuming it to be the suicidal note, it
was sent for examination to FSL, Dehradun;
however, there was no clear-cut opinion about the

signature of deceased thereon; thereafter, the said
document was again sent to the CFSL, Chandigarh;
thereafter, an application was recovered from the
documents of the Gurudwara which was allegedly
signed and written by the deceased, and that too was
sent to the CFSL, Chandigarh.
During investigation, facts revealed that the
said application was not actually signed by the
deceased and that was actually signed and written
by Jagtar Singh. As per the allegations of the
prosecution, the said application was actually
prepared on the instructions of the present accused.
It is a matter of evidence, whether or not, the
above application was actually prepared by Jagtar
Singh on the instructions of applicant, but it is true
that it was actually prepared by Jagtar Singh as per
the report of the CFSL, Chandigarh.
However, from a perusal of the evidence
collected during investigation, it is prima facie clear
that the signatures on the suicidal note, so
recovered, were not tallying with the signatures on
the salary register which was kept in the
Gurudwara. Now, again it is again a matter of
evidence whether the letter, so recovered from the
room of deceased, was actually a suicidal note or
not, and whether the application, which was said to
be prepared by Jagtar Singh, was actually prepared
at the instructions of applicant or not?
 However, without commenting any further on
the merits of the case, at this juncture, the applicant

has been able to make out a case for bail at this
stage.
 The bail application is thus, allowed and the
applicant is directed to be released on bail on his
executing a personal bond and furnishing two
reliable sureties, each of the like amount, to the
satisfaction of the Court concerned.
 Pending application, if any, stands disposed
of.
 The observations made hereinabove shall not
have any bearing on the final merits of the case.
 (R.C. Khulbe, J.)
 18.08.2021
Rdang
